classification.difficultyReason: Identify the perpendicular cross-section through a base-edge midpoint, then calculate its hypotenuse and inclination.

content.prompt:
The Great Pyramid of Giza is a square pyramid.

It has a perpendicular height of 280 royal cubits and a base length of 440 royal cubits.

Show that the apothem $(a)$ is around 356 royal cubits and it has an angle of inclination of $52^\circ$.

spec.description: Oblique square pyramid with unlabelled vertices, visible outlines, dashed hidden edges and base construction lines, perpendicular height and apothem. Red dimension labels are retained; faces are unshaded.
spec.mathematics: The height meets the centre of the square base. The apothem meets the midpoint of a base edge, so its horizontal run is 220 royal cubits. Base diagonals and the midpoint cross-section remain construction lines.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown a appear.

answer.worked:
The distance from the centre of the base to the midpoint of a base edge is $440\div2=220$ royal cubits.

$$\begin{aligned}a&=\sqrt{280^2+220^2}\\a&=\sqrt{126800}\\a&\approx356\text{ royal cubits}\end{aligned}$$

Let $\theta$ be the angle between the apothem and the horizontal base.

$$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{280}{220}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{280}{220}\right)\\\theta&\approx52^\circ\end{aligned}$$
